stories.body: Iran says it and Oman have reached an understanding on the geographic coordinates of a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz and are finalising a joint statement. The arrangement could help restore commercial traffic through the strategic waterway, where shipping has been severely disrupted, and could create space for wider negotiations between Tehran and Washington. Iranian officials say the agreement alone would not guarantee security, while US President Donald Trump has suggested a broader deal may be imminent.
stories.headline: Iran says Strait of Hormuz agreement with Oman is in its final stage

stories.body: Russian overnight attacks killed at least six people, with three deaths reported in Balakliia in the Kharkiv region and three in Sumy region. A Russian strike also damaged a foreign-flagged wheat ship in the Black Sea area, killing a crew member, Ukrainian officials said. The attacks come as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urges allies to speed up supplies of Patriot interceptors and other air defences, warning that Russia is increasing missile production ahead of winter.
stories.headline: Russian strikes kill at least six in Ukraine as Kyiv calls for more air defences

stories.body: German police deployed a bomb-disposal robot after an employee found a small drone carrying an explosive device near Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport. Authorities later conducted a controlled explosion, and a second unidentified object reportedly struck a cargo aircraft that had aborted a landing, causing minor damage before it landed safely in Hanover. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called the events a new level of danger and said investigators were examining a possible professional hybrid threat involving foreign powers.
stories.headline: Explosives-carrying drone found at Leipzig airport prompts major German security operation

stories.body: Nigeria says a coordinated intelligence-led operation rescued 308 people abducted in separate attacks in Niger and Kwara states, calling it the country’s largest single-day hostage rescue. Those freed included 163 people seized during a February attack on the Woro community in Kwara and 145 abductees from Niger State. The victims were recovered from the Kainji Lake National Park forest and were receiving medical care before reunification with their families.
stories.headline: Nigeria says it rescued 308 people abducted by armed groups

stories.body: Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated Representative Haley Stevens to win the Democratic nomination for the US Senate in Michigan, a major victory for the party’s progressive wing in a pivotal battleground state. El-Sayed, who would become the first Muslim US senator if elected, will face Republican former congressman Mike Rogers in November. The primary drew unusually high turnout and followed a contentious campaign shaped by arguments over Israel, immigration and health care.
stories.headline: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Democratic Senate primary in progressive upset

stories.body: An Associated Press review found that the Trump administration’s expanded immigration enforcement has detained more than 50 spouses and parents of active-duty US service members after ending protections that had previously been available to some military families. The cases have left service members facing deployments and military duties while partners or parents are held in immigration detention, raising concerns about the consequences for families and military readiness.
stories.headline: AP reports Trump immigration crackdown has detained more than 50 military spouses and parents

stories.body: A new report has confirmed that a spark from a utility tower caused California’s 2025 Eaton fire, corroborating longstanding suspicions about the blaze’s origin. Southern California Edison said it was reviewing the report.
stories.headline: Utility-tower spark confirmed as cause of California's 2025 Eaton fire

stories.body: Spanish authorities have begun individually identifying and processing migrants who remain in Ceuta after the mass crossing from Morocco, including determining who may seek international protection. The government says about 2,500 migrants remain in the city, while roughly 70,000 of the 72,000 people who entered on July 30 have returned to Morocco. Authorities are also preparing temporary accommodation and expect transfers of unaccompanied minors to mainland Spain to take months because of the scale of the arrivals.
stories.headline: Spain begins processing migrants and asylum claims after the Ceuta crossing crisis

stories.body: A judge at Spain’s National Court has asked the Civil Guard whether it received advance warnings about the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta on July 30 and 31. The inquiry also seeks details of rescue operations and fatalities, while police have been asked whether a criminal group helped organise the crossing. The request follows conflicting accounts from government, defence and Moroccan officials over whether Spain had been alerted to the risk of a major breach at the border.
stories.headline: Spanish court asks whether security forces had warning of the mass entry into Ceuta

stories.body: Police in Murcia arrested a man suspected of killing his 44-year-old former partner in the back room of a shopping-centre business after he fled the scene. Separately, a Civil Guard officer allegedly shot dead his former partner, also an officer, at the Llanes barracks in Asturias before dying after an exchange of fire with colleagues. Authorities are treating both cases as suspected gender-based killings; the alleged attacker in Asturias reportedly had open domestic-violence cases.
stories.headline: Two suspected gender-based killings reported in Murcia and at a Civil Guard barracks in Asturias

stories.body: Catalonia’s business and property groups are calling on the regional government to withdraw a proposed law restricting some home purchases and instead negotiate a broader housing pact. Their response follows a unanimous opinion by the Consell de Garanties Estatutàries that the proposal could violate property rights and business freedom, intrude on state powers and improperly alter civil law. The sector argues that policy should increase housing supply, provide legal certainty and encourage public-private cooperation.
stories.headline: Catalan housing sector calls for a pact after setback to anti-speculation law

stories.body: Barcelona firefighters evacuated workers from Bonfred SA, a food-logistics and cold-storage company at Mercabarna, after an ammonia leak was reported shortly after midnight. Eleven fire crews stopped and contained the leak, which originated in the building’s machinery room, and ventilated the facility. Civil Protection activated emergency plans, later deactivating them, and no injuries or intoxications were reported.
stories.headline: Ammonia leak at Mercabarna food logistics company forces precautionary evacuation

stories.body: Catalonia’s Civil Protection agency has activated the Inuncat flood emergency plan ahead of forecast thunderstorms on Thursday afternoon and evening. Meteocat warns that some areas could receive more than 40 litres of rain per square metre in 30 minutes and more than 60 litres in three hours, with strong winds, hail and possible violent weather. Authorities urged residents to avoid flood-prone areas, rivers and streams, limit travel during intense rain and follow official forecasts and instructions.
stories.headline: Catalunya activates flood alert ahead of potentially intense Thursday storms

stories.body: Barcelona has lost roughly one in four haberdasheries, drugstores and fishmongers since 2016, according to municipal business-location data, alongside declines in shoe shops, poultry and egg shops, and butcheries. The losses reflect pressure on traditional retail from changing consumer habits, supermarkets and lower-cost competitors, although the city’s overall number of active commercial premises has increased. The mayor has proposed regulating commercial rents and creating a fund to acquire endangered emblematic premises.
stories.headline: Barcelona loses a quarter of traditional haberdashery, drugstore and fishmonger businesses

stories.body: Eighteen flights were cancelled on the second day of an indefinite strike by Groundforce baggage-handling, check-in and boarding staff at Barcelona-El Prat Airport, adding to about 20 cancellations on the first day. The CGT union said participation among the company’s 1,179 workers remained very high and that no progress had been made in talks. The strike centres on what the union describes as deteriorating workplace health and safety conditions.
stories.headline: Barcelona airport ground-staff strike enters second day with 18 flights cancelled
